title: Théorie de Kumer ? + note Alexandre (bi tenseur…) : notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
This page is a working sketch for the theory of 'cartes' (maps on surfaces) that Grothendieck developed from about 1980 to 1984, which later became the 'dessins d'enfants' part of Esquisse d'un programme. It follows a page on universal pi-bundles and classifying spaces.

(1) Top line. A map is a triple x in X ⊃ K ⊃ S: a topological surface X, a 1-dimensional closed subspace K (the edges), and a finite set S (the vertices), with a base point (flag) x. The map has type (p,q), meaning bounded valencies and face degrees. Its universal cover (X~ ⊃ K~ ⊃ S~, x~) is identified with the universal map of type (p,q). This universal map is a torsor under the cartographic group C_pq, equivalently the triangle-type group Γ_pq acting on the sphere, the Euclidean plane or the hyperbolic plane. A given map then corresponds to a subgroup π ⊂ Γ_pq (its fundamental group). Its automorphism group is Norm(π)/π. This is the Galois-theoretic dictionary 'maps of type (p,q) = conjugacy classes of subgroups of the (p,q) cartographic group'.

(2) Hierarchy of groups. Γ_∞∞ ⊃ π is the case of no constraint, the free 'universal' cartographic group. It surjects onto Γ_∞,3 and onto Γ_p,q.
- Box at upper right: V ∋ e is the upper half-plane, viewed as the space of oriented bases (ω1, ω2) with Im(ω2/ω1) > 0.
- Middle column: a chain Γ_1 → Γ^0_∞,3 = SL(2,Z)/(±1) → S_3. This is the exact sequence 1 → Γ(2)/±1 → PSL(2,Z) → SL(2,Z/2) ≅ S_3 → 1.
- Picture of the sphere with three marked points: P^1 minus {0,1,∞}, the λ-line, uniformised by Γ(2).
- Left column: C_∞,3 → sphere → disk with marked points 0 and '2^?·3^?' plus a boundary point ∞. This is the j-line, with elliptic points j = 0 and j = 1728 and the cusp. It depicts PSL(2,Z) = Z/2 * Z/3 as the oriented group of trivalent maps.
- The relation ρ_s^3 = 1 and the generators {σ0, σ1, σ2} are the cartographic generators, with ρ_s the rotation about a vertex.
- Γ_∞3 ⊃ π, ρ_s, ρ_s^p: imposing ρ_s^p = 1 gives the quotient C_∞3 → C_p3.

(3) Bottom. For p'|p and q'|q there are quotient maps Γ_p,q → Γ_p',q' and C_pq → C_p'q' = C_pq/R, where R is the normal subgroup generated by the extra relations. The degenerate cases C_21, C_12 and C_11 are listed.

The problem served: setting up the cartographic groups as an inverse system indexed by (p,q) under divisibility, and identifying the trivalent/modular case with PSL(2,Z) and the modular curve. The next page then treats 'cartes trouées' and standard punctured disks D_n^*.
errors: The value written next to 0 on the j-line disk reads like 2^3·3^3 (= 216) in the machine transcription. The elliptic point is j = 1728 = 2^6·3^3, so either the transcription is wrong or Grothendieck slipped on the exponent.
The sequence Γ_1 → Γ^0_∞,3 → S_3 is only sketched with arrows. Correctly it is 1 → Γ(2)/±1 → PSL(2,Z) → S_3 → 1, with Γ(2)/±1 free of rank 2. No error, but it is not stated as exact.
The labels C_∞,3 versus C_p3 / ρ_s^3 = 1 mix conventions: here 3 is the order of the vertex rotation (trivalent case). This is a notational ambiguity, not a mathematical error.

ideas.what: Maps on surfaces (with base flag) of type (p,q) correspond to subgroups of a cartographic/triangle group; the universal cover of a map is the universal map; automorphisms = Norm(π)/π
ideas.modern_name: Correspondence between maps/dessins and subgroups of (2,p,q) triangle groups / cartographic groups
ideas.usually_credited_to: Jones & Singerman (1978); Malgoire & Voisin (1977); Grothendieck (Esquisse d'un programme, 1984)
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (1984), section on dessins d'enfants / cartographic groups

ideas.what: Oriented trivalent maps ↔ subgroups of PSL(2,Z) = Z/2*Z/3; universal cover = upper half-plane of oriented period bases; quotient = j-line with special points 0, 1728, ∞
ideas.modern_name: Trivalent maps and finite-index subgroups of the modular group
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical (Klein); in map theory Jones–Singerman, Grothendieck's Esquisse
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme (identification of C_2^+ with modular-group-related groups)

ideas.what: Γ(2)/±1 ⊂ PSL(2,Z) with quotient S_3, giving the λ-line P^1 − {0,1,∞}
ideas.modern_name: Principal congruence subgroup of level 2 / Legendre λ-function

ideas.what: Inverse system C_pq → C_p'q' = C_pq/R for p'|p, q'|q, including degenerate types C_21, C_12, C_11
ideas.modern_name: Quotients of triangle groups / profinite-type tower of cartographic groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse discusses C_2 and quotients; this explicit (p,q) divisibility system is only in notes as far as known

deep.surprise_reason: These are standard working notes for the cartographic-group / dessins theory that Grothendieck published in outline in Esquisse d'un programme. The content had already been developed independently by Jones–Singerman and Malgoire–Voisin. Nothing goes beyond the known dictionary.
transcription_corrections: '0  2^3.3^3' is the j-line's elliptic points: should read 0 and 1728 (= 2^6·3^3). The exponents as written in the image are hard to read.
'R q_1(q'_1,q_1')' likely reads 'R(p,q;p',q')' or similar, denoting the relations defining C_pq → C_p'q'.
'Γ_{p,q} ↓ Γ_{p',q'}' at bottom left is written 'Γ_{p,q} → Γ_{p',q'}' (a vertical arrow) in the image.
'Γ_{22}' in the middle right appears to label the hatched-sphere picture; it may refer to the (2,2) type.
'V∋e' is part of a box describing the space of period bases (ω1, ω2) with Im(ω2/ω1) > 0.
